Perspective / September 12, 2026 / 4 min read

The art of leaving things out.

Why the most memorable digital experiences often say less.

Attention is a design material.

Every element asks for something: a glance, a decision, a moment of attention. When everything competes at once, the work loses its voice. Restraint starts with deciding what deserves to be noticed.

Give the important things room.

Whitespace is not empty. It establishes relationships between ideas and creates a pace for the reader. A single image with a precise caption can communicate more than a wall of competing messages. The question is not how much a page can contain, but what a person needs to understand next.

Remove with intention.

Start with the core purpose of a page. Keep the content that supports it. Challenge repeated explanations, decorative controls, and motion that does not clarify an action. A quieter interface should still be generous with the information people actually need.

A useful final test.

Read the page aloud. Follow its links with a keyboard. Look at it on a small screen. If the hierarchy still holds, the restraint is doing useful work. Luxury is often the confidence to stop before adding one more thing.
